why: In some children ADA deficiency can be cured by bone marrow transplantation; in others it can be treated by enzyme replacement therapy, in which functional ADA is given to the patient by injection. The binding of the substrate induces the enzyme to alter its shape, fitting more tightly around the substrate. 3. The active site of the enzyme, now in close proximity of the substrate breaks the chemical bonds of the substrate and the new enzyme- product complex is formed. 4. The enzyme releases the products of the reaction and the free enzyme is ready to bind to another molecule of the substrate and run through the catalytic cycle once again.

why: RNA interference (RNAi) is a gene-silencing mechanism used by cells to regulate gene expression or defend against viral RNA. It works through double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) that is complementary to the target mRNA. This is how it works: Introduction of complementary dsRNA into the cell. The dsRNA is recognized and cleaved by an enzyme called Dicer into small fragments called siRNA (small interfering RNA). These siRNAs bind to a protein complex called RISC (RNA-induced silencing complex). The siRNA guides RISC to the complementary mRNA, leading to its cleavage and silencing (i.e., preventing translation). Therefore, complementary double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) is crucial for initiating RNAi.
